title: Closed-Quarter OTC Forfeiture — Benefit Accounting Worksheet
content:
**Pharmacy Benefit, OTC allowance ledger.** The forfeiture booked when a benefit quarter closes is worked out as follows.

### Definitions

1. **Closed quarter.** The closed quarter is the benefit quarter of the latest allowance load on the coverage.
2. **Amount loaded.** The total of the allowance load entries tagged to the closed quarter.
3. **Purchases.** The total of every purchase tagged to the closed quarter.
4. **Quarter's unused allowance.** The quarter's unused allowance is the amount loaded for the closed quarter less every purchase tagged to the closed quarter, never below zero.

### The forfeiture

The closed-quarter forfeiture is the whole unused allowance of the closed quarter, and nothing of it is carried into the next quarter. Only the closed-quarter forfeiture is rounded to the cent; the figures that lead to it are carried unrounded.

### Worksheet layout

| Line | Entry |
|---|---|
| A | Amount loaded for the closed quarter |
| B | Purchases tagged to the closed quarter |
| C | Unused allowance: A less B, never below zero |
| D | Forfeiture: C, rounded to the cent |

### Worked figures (hypothetical)

| | Case 1 | Case 2 |
|---|---|---|
| A — loaded for the closed quarter | $50.00 | $25.00 |
| B — purchases tagged to it | $31.25 and $6.10, total $37.35 | $26.40 |
| C — unused allowance | $12.65 | $0.00 (never below zero) |
| D — forfeiture | $12.65 | $0.00 |

In Case 1 the forfeiture of $12.65 lowers the allowance balance by $12.65, and nothing of the closed quarter's allowance remains on the balance.
